items.content: The tide went out slowly, indifferently, taking its colour with it — the greens and silvers and the brief brightness of the reflected late sun — until what remained was wet sand, dark and patient, stippled with the holes of things that had retreated. She stood at the waterline and watched the world shrink. There is a version of loss, she thought, that does not ask your permission.
items.explanation: Generated by Claude claude-sonnet-4-6 about "watching the tide go out at dusk". The polished structure and conceptually inventive metaphors are characteristic of language model output.

items.content: After the last door closed, the house had a different quality — not empty exactly, but relieved of its obligation to be a house. The chairs stood at their angles. The dishes drained. The rooms were no longer performing themselves, and so they could be, briefly, what they actually were: large boxes of accumulated time, full of air and the shapes of people who were somewhere else.
items.explanation: Generated by Claude claude-sonnet-4-6 about "the particular silence of a house after everyone has left". AI text often produces grammatically perfect sentences with slightly generic emotional beats — look for overly balanced structure and lack of truly surprising word choices.

items.content: In my younger and more vulnerable years my father gave me some advice that I've been turning over in my mind ever since.
items.explanation: Fitzgerald's narrator Nick Carraway, introducing himself with deliberate restraint. The confessional register and withheld detail are signatures of Fitzgerald's distinctly human voice.
items.source: F. Scott Fitzgerald — The Great Gatsby (1925)

items.content: The smell rose from the pavement with the first drops — something ancient and mineral, released from the stone by the heat, half-chemical, half-alive. She stopped on the sidewalk and breathed it in without deciding to. Around her, others paused too, briefly, before continuing — each of them ambushed by the same involuntary memory of other summers, other rain, other versions of themselves standing in the warmth and smelling the earth come back.
items.explanation: Generated by Claude claude-sonnet-4-6 about "the smell of rain on hot pavement in summer". Notice the even pacing and absence of the kinds of small errors or tonal shifts that appear in prose written under genuine emotional pressure.
